evidence_class: posthoc robustness audit of already-opened community-insurance endpoint
motivation: The pooled exact-point analysis found higher retained seagrass occupancy after Thalassia loss when another seagrass was already present. Test whether the binary mixed-versus-Thalassia-only association persists within stable transect nodes rather than mainly reflecting persistent site quality.

source.transition_population: exact same 370 transitions used by results/community_insurance_v1.json

primary_population.rule: retain stable nodes containing at least one source_mixed=true and at least one source_mixed=false transition

predictor.note: binary mixed-versus-Thalassia-only state; do not replace with richness after opening this audit

model: logistic regression: target_any_seagrass_present ~ standardized target_year + standardized within_node_centered_source_mixed + node_id fixed effects; sklearn LogisticRegression C=1.0 lbfgs, matching the existing diversity node audit reference-saturation framework

uncertainty.method: stable-node cluster bootstrap; all transitions from sampled nodes travel together and duplicated clusters receive distinct bootstrap node labels
uncertainty.support_rule: 95% bootstrap interval for standardized centered source-mixed coefficient entirely above zero

secondary_descriptive: number of informative nodes and transitions
node-level mixed-minus-alone occupancy differences where both outcomes/groups are observed

interpretation.supported: The mixed-versus-alone occupancy-retention association persists after stable-node saturation; this strengthens a microsite-scale community-insurance interpretation but remains observational and does not prove facilitation.
interpretation.unsupported: The pooled mixed-versus-alone association is not robust after stable-node saturation; persistent transect quality remains a plausible explanation and the retrospective result should be framed as pooled state association rather than demonstrated local insurance.

claim_boundary: Do not call this causal biodiversity insurance or facilitation.
Do not infer functional equivalence from retained occupancy.
Do not change the node eligibility rule, predictor, model, bootstrap unit, or support threshold after opening the result.
Do not subset by bay, species identity, or year to rescue an unsupported primary.
